scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Rejang is an ancient sacred Balinese dance, conceived as a sacrificial offering in which girls present themselves before Hindu deities.
Practiced across Hindu sanctuaries in Bali, the dance forms a core element of cyclic religious calendar rites designed to greet divine spirits descending to Earth.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The word 'Rejang' translates directly to 'offering'.
It serves as a greeting ceremony for gods arriving on Earth during major milestones of the Balinese ceremonial calendar.
The act embodies the concept of ngayah, or spiritual community service and devotion.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance takes the form of a harmonious procession.
Participants undergo no prior formal training, believing that the spirit of ngayah guides their bodies to move in complete unison.
Girls as young as two or three years old join the communal line, moving together under shared devotion.
on_screen: Formation: Procession through temple grounds and the village hall of Bale Agung.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Rejang is conducted within Hindu temple grounds, notably in Klungkung Regency and Karangasem Regency.
Its primary staging takes place during three-day ceremonies organized at the Bale Agung, the communal village hall.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The dance carries local variant names across communities, known alternately as ngeremas, Simi, or sutri.
Rejang belongs to the sacred category of Balinese temple dances, sharing cultural and regional lineage with traditions such as Pendet, Joged, and Janger.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Rejang is a sacred sacrificial dance where girls offer themselves to descending Hindu deities; it must remain within its proper ceremonial context and should not be treated as casual entertainment.

scenes.title: Until next time
